official_sources.title: Environment Agency LIDAR Composite DTM 1m
official_sources.finding: The 1m DTM removes surface objects from the DSM using bespoke algorithms and manual editing, combines Time Stamped and National LIDAR Programme surveys, and may use bilinear resampling before merge.

official_sources.title: Environment Agency LIDAR Composite DSM 1m
official_sources.finding: The DSM includes vehicles, buildings and vegetation as well as terrain, so DSM extrema cannot substitute for ground-terrain extrema.

official_sources.title: Environment Agency LIDAR Composite DTM 10m
official_sources.finding: The 10m DTM is bilinearly resampled from the 2m composite, so its cells are derived interpolated values rather than native highest-resolution terrain samples.

official_sources.title: Environment Agency LIDAR Composite DTM 2m
official_sources.finding: The 2m composite removes surface objects and merges/re-samples multiple surveys; metadata catalogues identify which survey contributes at a location.

official_sources.title: Environment Agency DTM Time Stamped Tiles
official_sources.finding: Time Stamped DTM tiles are site-specific terrain rasters at 25cm/50cm/1m/2m, remove surface objects, are in metres referenced to Ordnance Datum Newlyn, and report +/-15cm RMSE vertical accuracy.

official_sources.title: Environment Agency DSM Time Stamped Tiles
official_sources.finding: Time Stamped DSM tiles include vehicles, buildings and vegetation, providing an explicit semantic contrast to terrain-only DTM products.

official_sources.title: Environment Agency Time Stamped Point Cloud
official_sources.finding: The point-cloud archive carries x,y,z and attributes, underlies site-specific DSM/DTM rasters, and classifies returns into ground and surface objects; historic raster products may not always have matching archived point clouds.

official_sources.title: Environment Agency National LIDAR Programme
official_sources.finding: England was divided into 302 survey blocks, with phase-1 surveys captured over winters from 2017 to 2023 and later repeat phases driven by update needs; survey phase/date therefore belong in lineage.

official_sources.title: Environment Agency First Return DSM 2m
official_sources.finding: First-return DSM contains object tops and terrain where first return is ground, uses feathering across survey overlaps, and reports survey-level vertical accuracy; it is not a bare-earth DTM.

official_sources.title: Environment Agency LIDAR Mapping Collection
official_sources.finding: Environment Agency describes lidar as measuring both terrain and surface objects and identifies its DTM as the terrain product for slope/contour/topographic use.

official_sources.title: Environment Agency LIDAR Tile Catalogues
official_sources.finding: Official catalogue layers separately expose DTM and DSM time-stamped extents in EPSG:27700, supporting location-specific survey-product lineage checks.

official_sources.title: USGS Lidar Base Specification Tables
official_sources.finding: USGS minimum classification distinguishes bare earth class 2, water class 9, bridge deck class 17, ignored ground class 20 and noise classes; DEM quality level also constrains cell size and vertical accuracy.

official_sources.title: USGS Lidar Base Specification Deliverables
official_sources.finding: Bare-earth DEMs use ground-classified non-withheld points, encode voids as NODATA, remove bridges, preserve roads over culverts, hydroflatten water, and require PixelIsArea.

official_sources.title: USGS DEM Surface Treatments
official_sources.finding: Bare-earth terrain below bridges is a logical interpolation from surrounding apparent terrain; breakline-near points may be classified ignored ground to prevent artifacts.

official_sources.title: USGS Hydro-Flattening Reference
official_sources.finding: Hydro-flattened topographic DEMs represent actual ground surface while treating water cartographically; USGS explicitly does not assert accuracy for lidar water-surface elevations.

official_sources.title: USGS Lidar Base Specification Glossary
official_sources.finding: Lidar classification differentiates bare-earth terrain, water, noise, vegetation, buildings and other objects; DEM cells represent numeric information for an area rather than exact surveyed vertices.

official_sources.title: USGS Collection Requirements
official_sources.finding: USGS defines pulse-density/spacing thresholds and treats sufficiently large first-return coverage gaps as data voids, making source coverage completeness a prerequisite.

official_sources.title: USGS Data Processing and Handling Requirements
official_sources.finding: Vertical accuracy must be validated before derivative products, classification must be consistent across project divisions, and tiled raster products must align and edge-match without gaps.

official_sources.title: USGS Standardized Breakline Delivery
official_sources.finding: Breaklines used to generate DEMs are required deliverables and must allow the DEM to be recreated from lidar points and breaklines without substantial editing.

official_sources.title: USGS Lidar Figures
official_sources.finding: USGS examples identify insufficient swath coverage as data voids and grounds for rejection, reinforcing fail-closed coverage handling.

official_sources.title: USGS Lidar Base Specification Revision History
official_sources.finding: 2025 revisions added ignored-ground handling for near-vertical/overhanging surfaces, snow classification requirements and raster-type consistency, demonstrating that processing semantics are versioned provenance.

official_sources.title: USGS Updated Accuracy Standards Adoption
official_sources.finding: USGS updated lidar reporting to newer ASPRS positional-accuracy standards; accuracy terminology and reporting basis must be version-pinned rather than assumed constant.

official_sources.title: USGS Standards Templates and Examples
official_sources.finding: USGS publishes standardized breakline, metadata and error-dictionary artifacts to support consistent lidar QA and provenance.

official_sources.title: GDAL Working with a DTM
official_sources.finding: GDAL treats a DTM as the input elevation raster for clipping and terrain derivatives such as hillshade, slope and aspect; those derivatives remain downstream products, not replacement elevation values.

official_sources.title: GDAL Raster Slope
official_sources.finding: Slope is derived from a 3x3 elevation neighborhood and may interpolate near edges/nodata by default, so slope outputs cannot substitute for native DTM extrema.

official_sources.title: GDAL Raster Aspect
official_sources.finding: Aspect is another derived terrain raster with algorithm and edge-interpolation choices, reinforcing separation of base elevation from derivative morphology.

official_sources.title: GDAL Raster Commands
official_sources.finding: GDAL explicitly separates fill-nodata, slope, aspect, roughness, TRI/TPI and other derived raster operations from the original raster dataset.

official_sources.title: GDAL DEM Processing
official_sources.finding: DEM terrain analyses have algorithm, unit-scaling and edge-computation options, so their outputs are method-dependent derivatives rather than authoritative elevations.

official_sources.title: Environment Agency DTM 1m Defra Record
official_sources.finding: The official Defra record confirms composite DTM survey provenance varies by location and points users to metadata-index catalogues to identify the contributing survey.

official_sources.title: USGS Lidar Base Specification References
official_sources.finding: USGS anchors current lidar processing/accuracy requirements to published LAS, ASPRS and related standards, so standards-version provenance must accompany terminal QA.
